findings.title: Rapid app foreground events can interleave network probes and flip online state to a stale result
findings.why_it_matters: The network provider listens to AppState changes and runs a polling interval. A user switching apps rapidly, or the OS bouncing between active/inactive during a permission prompt, can trigger overlapping probeNetwork calls. Because checkNow does not serialize in-flight probes, a slow stale failure can overwrite a recent success and incorrectly show the user as offline.
evidence: apps/mobile/src/providers/network-provider.tsx:78 checkNow is called by mount effect, interval, and AppState listener
apps/mobile/src/providers/network-provider.tsx:64 consecutiveFailuresRef and setState are read/written from asynchronous handlers without a generation guard
findings.suggested_fix: Add an isProbingRef guard that returns early when a probe is in flight, or track a probe generation ID and ignore results from older probes.

findings.title: Sign-out during an active Convex mutation can strand the mutation in flight while auth is cleared
findings.why_it_matters: A user can tap sign-out while a mutation (e.g., scheduling an activity) is pending. signOut clears Convex auth immediately, but the in-flight mutation may still hold a valid JWT and attempt to write data. After the mutation resolves, the UI may show a success toast and then redirect to login, leaving the user uncertain whether the action completed.
evidence: apps/mobile/src/providers/auth-provider.tsx:117 signOut dispatches SIGN_OUT_REQUEST and proceeds to clearSecureAuthStorage + convexClient.clearAuth()
No global pending-mutation barrier or cancellation is visible in the provider or screens
findings.suggested_fix: Queue sign-out behind pending mutations, cancel in-flight mutations before clearing auth, or at least surface a 'sign-out blocked while saving' message until pending work finishes.

findings.title: Malformed or cross-table invoice id from deep link crashes before backend can reject it
findings.why_it_matters: A universal link, push notification, or manually constructed URL can supply any string as the invoice id. The screen casts it to Id<'invoices'> and passes it to useQuery. If the string is not a valid Convex Id, the query may throw an unexpected error that the ErrorBoundary catches, but the cast itself bypasses TypeScript and any client-side guard.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate the id string against Convex's id format (or at least ensure it is non-empty and well-formed) before casting. Pass a validated typed id to the query.

findings.title: Token revocation clears storage but not the active Convex WebSocket auth
findings.why_it_matters: When useSession returns an error, the provider scrubs secure storage and dispatches TOKEN_REVOKED. However, it does not call convexClient.clearAuth(). The existing WebSocket connection may remain authenticated with its current JWT until the token expires, allowing a small window where a revoked session can still read data.
findings.suggested_fix: Also call convexClient.clearAuth() in the TOKEN_REVOKED path so the WebSocket connection re-authenticates (or becomes unauthenticated) immediately.

findings.title: Concurrent sign-in button presses can dispatch multiple SIGN_IN_REQUEST events and submit multiple login calls
findings.why_it_matters: The login screen's submit handler does not appear to disable the button or guard against double-tap while the auth machine is in the 'signingIn' state. A user rapidly tapping the button, or assistive-tech repeat, can trigger multiple signIn.email calls. This creates unnecessary load and may produce confusing error states if the first call succeeds and the second fails with an invalid-credential message.
evidence: Auth machine has isAuthBusy but no visible guard in the UI handler
findings.suggested_fix: Disable the login submit button while status === 'signingIn', or add an early return in the submit handler when isAuthBusy(state.status) is true.

residual_risks: A malicious or misconfigured deep link could pass an id belonging to another organization. If the backend query lacks an org-scoped filter, this becomes an IDOR vulnerability.
If the user backgrounds the app during sign-out, the finally block may run when the app is backgrounded and SecureStore operations could fail silently, leaving tokens on disk.
The network banner's 'Retry' path is a no-op in activities/index.tsx; users on a flaky connection have no way to force a refetch other than navigating away and back.
testing_gaps: Adversarial test: rapidly toggle AppState and assert the final network state reflects the most recent probe, not an older stale one.
Adversarial test: invoke signOut while a mutation is pending and verify either the mutation completes and then logout happens, or the mutation is cancelled and the user is informed.
Adversarial test: pass malformed and cross-table ids to invoice detail and assert graceful handling.
